newsitem.title: UK: UK's Nat Grid, Nat Power win pensions surplus case.
newsitem.headline: UK's Nat Grid, Nat Power win pensions surplus case.

text.p: A British court on Tuesday backed electricity transmission company National Grid Group Plc and generator National Power Plc over their use of pensions surpluses to fund redundancy payments.
Mr Justice Robert Walker allowed an appeal by National Grid against a decision by Britain's pensions ombudsman that it should return 43 million pounds ($70.3 million).
He also ruled that the arrangements made by National Power had been valid and effective. If he had ruled against the firm it could have been asked to pay back as much as 200 million pounds.

The judge acknowledged his ruling would be disappointing for the two former National Grid employees who had challenged it and many other pensioners of both groups who had hoped for benefits to their pensions after the ombudsman's ruling.
"This is a disappointment not just to me but to all those people who are calling for justice," David Laws, 59, said outside London's High Court.
"Eventually we will get justice," he added. Laws and Reg Mayes, 73, were given leave to appeal the ruling and said they would pursue the matter to the appeal court if they could get funding.

One legal expert estimated the total cost of the cases so far at more than a million pounds, although the expense of taking them to appeal would not be as great as most of the groundwork had been done.
The two companies have until now funded legal costs of the trustees of the pension funds, Mayes, Laws and Howard Machin, who represented the National Power pension fund members.
In a lengthy ruling, the judge said the ombudsman's decision had been based "on a misunderstanding of the terms of the scheme and of the employers' duties in dealing with surplus."
National Grid had appealed pension ombudsman Julian Farrand's judgement in February which said the privatised firm should repay the surplus cash taken from the pension fund.

Walker said the decisions reached by National Grid and National Power over the use of the surplus had "brought significant benefit improvements for pensioners, pensioners' families and active members" and were "reasonable and proper decisions".
National Power and National Grid both welcomed the court decision.
But Laws said if the ruling stood it would leave pensioners exposed to the dangers of high inflation wiping out the value of their pensions, which would no longer have a surplus to back them up.
"It's a pension fund and clearly it should not be used in the employer's interest," he said.($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
